newsitem.title: USA: Clinton says unsure if he raised funds by phone.
newsitem.headline: Clinton says unsure if he raised funds by phone.

text.p: President Bill Clinton said on Friday he could not remember whether he may have solicited campaign funds by telephone from the White House, a practice that has opened Vice President Al Gore to criticism.

"I can't say that over all the hundreds and hundreds, maybe thousands of phone calls I've made in the past four years, that I never said to anybody while I was talking to them, 'well, we need your help,' or 'I hope you'll help us,'" Clinton said at a news conference. He added that he had therefore told his spokesman, if asked about the issue, "not to flat out say that I'd never done it because I simply can't say that I've never done it."

Clinton commented at a news conference turned into a virtual interrogation on the fund-raising controversy that is engulfing the White House. He insisted he and his aides had broken no laws but were compelled to compete fiercely with Republicans for election campaign money by a political system that puts a premium on heavy spending.

He specifically defended Gore from charges he may have broken a law against raising political cash on federal property by soliciting support by telephone from his White House office. Gore has said he did not violate such laws and Clinton backed him up on that interpretation.
He was then asked whether he had made any such calls himself and admitted he could not flatly state he had not.
He added: "It's not what I like to do and it wasn't a practice of mine ... But, I don't believe the vice president did anything wrong by making the calls."
